name: PT Andira Agro, Tbk

frontmatter.title: Andira Agro — a FFB processor running far below its estate, after the control change
frontmatter.summary: Andira Agro processed fresh fruit bunches and sold CPO and palm kernel. FY2025 lost money on a purchased-FFB model; the nine months to September 2026 show a much smaller crop, a positive gross margin and a going-concern note. Our base case holds the post-pivot crop flat: no contract, FFB-supply agreement or company plan in the archived filings supports a return to FY2025 volume. We initiate at SELL: the price discounts a recovery the filings do not support, not the pivot the filings show.
thesis: **Volume** — CPO volume falls to 2.4 kt CPO in FY2026E from 13.9 kt CPO in FY2025A after the 2026 contraction, and the base holds it flat to 2.4 kt CPO; the planted core and plasma estate explain capability, not recovery [S6, S5].

**Realisation** — the 83.2% discount to the CPO deck persists; the gross margin turned positive on the product mix, with kernel and shell revenue now exceeding CPO revenue in 9M 2026, not on price [S6].

**Costs** — per-tonne cash cost is roughly flat at 16,100,000.0 USD/t against FY2025; EBITDA is positive at IDR18.8bn but EBIT negative at IDR-7.6bn because D&A of IDR26.3bn was built for a much larger crop [S4, S6].

**Leverage** — net debt of IDR141.0bn exceeds the DCF equity value, so at any normal multiple the equity is out of the money; the bank facility matures in 2029 and no source of new capital is disclosed [S4, S6].

catalysts.event: Any new-controller funding or debt-restructuring announcement

blocks.text: **SELL — target Rp11, -61.2% versus the Rp29 price.** Andira Agro is a small South Sumatran palm-oil processor that buys fresh fruit bunches (FFB) from nucleus, plasma and third-party growers and sells crude palm oil (CPO) and palm kernel (PK). It is not a fully integrated planter: the FY2025 accounts show raw-material purchases dominating cost of revenue, and the core estate's HGU certificates are pledged to the bank facility, with title risk concentrated in the plasma land and HGU expiry [S5, S4, S6]. That structure made FY2025 a loss-making year at the operating line (IDR-27.5bn) despite revenue of IDR246.4bn [S4].

The last actual is not FY2025 but the nine months to September 2026. Revenue in that period collapsed against the prior-year comparative (IDR63.1bn net sales) while gross profit turned positive at IDR13.4bn [S6]. The segment split is the key: CPO revenue was IDR29.7bn and PK/shell revenue IDR33.3bn in the period [S6, note 38], so the by-product line now earns more than the main product and the whole cost of sales is allocated to CPO. We model that post-pivot mix, not a return to the old trading volume. The base case carries CPO volume of 2.4 kt CPO in FY2026E, held flat to 2.4 kt CPO by FY2030E, against 13.9 kt CPO in FY2025A [S6, S4].

The variant view is that the market is capitalising the old revenue base and the control-change story, not the shrunken cash-generating unit. At Rp29 the shares trade on 2.7x book, for a company whose base-case EBITDA of IDR18.8bn is swallowed by IDR26.3bn of depreciation and IDR11.6bn of interest, with net debt of IDR141.0bn and no dividend [S4, S6]. Our DCF puts the equity at Rp7 on the primary method; the P/B cross-check at 1.3x sits above it and we keep it only as a trading-multiple check, at 20.0% weight, so the base-case value is Rp9. Weighting the bear, base and bull scenarios at their probabilities gives the twelve-month target of Rp11. The three things that move the value are the CPO deck (1,240.0 USD/t in FY2027E), the volume the new controller can restore, and the cost of refinancing the bank debt [S4, S6].

We initiate at **SELL**. The strongest case against us is a new-owner recapitalisation that restores part of the lost FFB supply and lifts volume materially above the flat base — still a fraction of the FY2025 crop; the filings do not yet support even that, so it sits in the bull case (Rp23, probability 25.0%), not the base [S6].

PT Andira Agro Tbk was founded in 1995, listed on the IDX in 2018 and is based in East Jakarta, with its mill and estates in Banyuasin, South Sumatra [S0, S5]. It operates two reported segments, CPO and palm kernel, and describes its activity as cultivating and harvesting FFB and extracting CPO and PK from it [S0, S5]. [S0,S5] The workforce is small: 68.0 employees at the last count [S0], consistent with a single-mill operation that relies on purchased FFB rather than a large estate labour force.

FY2025 production was 87.2 kt of FFB processed, 13.9 kt CPO of CPO and some palm kernel [S5]. CPO is the dominant revenue line: the segment note shows CPO revenue of IDR191.2bn against IDR55.2bn for PK and shells in FY2025 [S4]. The customer mix is not disclosed by name; the accounts show trade receivables, so sales are largely cash or short-dated [S4]. [S5,S4]

The ownership structure matters. At 30 September 2026 the register showed PT Central Energi Pratama holding the largest block and PT Anugerah Perkasa Semesta the second largest, with the remaining 31.2% free float [S6, S0]. In October 2026 press reports said Puncak Jaya Sejahtera had bought the Central Energi Pratama block, making it the new controller; the company's disclosure page lists no filing on the transfer (press, not filed) [S7]. The company holds HGU certificates for the core estate: the bank-loan collateral note lists the HGU certificates pledged to Bank Permata, and the deferred land-rights note records HGU No. 16 as issued in 2010 [S6, notes 12 and 21]. The risk flagged in the FY2025 annual report is HGU expiry and delays in the plasma-land process, not an absence of certificates. That structural weakness nevertheless remains: the land rights behind the mature plantations matter for any asset-based valuation [S6, S5].

Strategy in the FY2025 report is explicitly efficiency-led: repair of damaged infrastructure, better FFB collection and use of an advisor to raise CPO and PK extraction [S5]. The 9M 2026 result is the first evidence of that strategy: lower revenue, but a positive gross margin and a much smaller operating loss [S6]. The company is a price-taker in both FFB and CPO; it has no branded product, no downstream refining and no material export franchise disclosed [S4, S5].

The operating footprint is one mill and its surrounding estates in Banyuasin. The land tenure is a PIR-Trans KKPA scheme: 4,743.6 of core land and 4,965.7 of plasma land farmed by transmigrant families, with long-term contracts with cooperatives and third parties in the district for plantation development and maintenance [S6, S5]. The mill can process 30.0 tonnes of FFB per hour [S5], and FY2025 output included 4,448.7 tonnes of palm kernel alongside the CPO [S5]. That is small by national standards, but it is a real processing licence with a defined catchment, which is why we do not value the operation at zero even though it earns below its cost of capital.

Indonesia is the world's largest palm-oil producer. The FY2025 annual report cites national planted area and CPO output for 2024 with output rising in 2025, at an average productivity of a few tonnes of CPO per hectare [S5]. The house agri deck carries CPO at 1,007.0 USD/t for FY2025A, 1,135.0 USD/t for FY2026E and 1,240.0 USD/t for FY2027E, with a long-run marker of 1,150.0 USD/t [S0 deck].

The industry drivers that matter for Andira are: (i) the CPO price, which sets its selling price with a fixed quality and location discount; (ii) the FFB supply chain, because the mill's utilisation depends on nucleus, plasma and third-party growers; (iii) the export levy and biodiesel mandate, which change the wedge between domestic and export CPO; and (iv) the weather, which drives the FFB crop and therefore the fruit price the mill pays [S5]. None of these is within the company's control, and its small scale means no pricing power.

Competitive position is weak. Andira is a challenger among Indonesian planters: its CPO output of 13.9 kt CPO is a fraction of the output of the listed integrated majors, and it does not own the land or the FFB base that would give it a cost advantage [S5, S4]. The FY2025 segment note splits cost of revenue between CPO and PK, each carrying a small gross loss [S4, note 38]; in the nine months to September 2026 the whole cost of sales is posted against the CPO revenue line while the PK and shell revenue line carries none [S6, note 38]. That is the signature of a processor buying FFB for more than the CPO it extracts is worth: the CPO segment bears the whole cost, not the by-products [S6, S4]. The moat, if any, is the mill's location and the plasma relationships around it; that is a thin moat and it has not protected returns.

Five forces: supplier power is high (fragmented FFB growers can sell elsewhere, and the company has acknowledged shortages and delays [S5]); buyer power is high (CPO is a commodity with published reference prices); new entrants are possible but capital-intensive; substitutes are limited in food and oleochemicals; and rivalry is intense among many small mills. Regulation is a material external influence: export levies, the B40/B50 biodiesel programme and land-title rules all bear on the economics, and HGU renewal and the plasma-land title chain are the company's regulatory exposures [S5, S6]. We therefore treat the industry as structurally cyclical and the company as a price-taker with below-average cost position.

Regulation and demand set the frame. The FY2025 report sets out the company's membership of GAPKI and its ISPO certification and describes the sustainability standards the sector is expected to meet [S5]. For a processor that buys FFB rather than owning a large estate, the levy matters on both sides of the trade, the price paid for fruit and the price received for oil, so the wedge matters more than the level. On the cost curve Andira is a small, single-mill, high-cost operator with no refinery and no export franchise; it sits in the higher-cost part of the Indonesian curve, which is why it earns a thin or negative margin at deck prices while integrated majors earn a normal return [S4, S5].

**History.** Revenue rose from IDR196.7bn in FY2024A to IDR246.4bn in FY2025A, but cost of revenue rose faster, to IDR250.0bn, producing a gross loss of IDR-3.5bn [S4]. The operating loss was IDR-27.5bn on the LK presentation, which carries the one-off other income below the operating line (mostly a non-cash reversal of a receivable allowance and a gain on asset disposal) [S4]. EBITDA on our restated basis was IDR2.8bn; the data pack's D&A is only the opex slice of a IDR30.4bn total charge, which is why we restate the line from the notes [S4].

**The 9M 2026 pivot.** Revenue for the nine months to September 2026 was down sharply, with cost of revenue also down and a gross profit turning positive [S6]. Operating expenses were materially lower and the operating loss narrowed from the year earlier; the net loss shrank after lower interest expense [S6]. This is a lower-volume, higher-margin business on the observed run-rate: no filing states a structural change in FFB sourcing, so we assume none and carry the nine-month unit economics forward [S6].

**Forecast.** We model FY2026E revenue of IDR81.7bn, EBITDA of IDR18.8bn, EBIT of IDR-7.6bn and a net loss of IDR-19.2bn [S6, S4]. The volume anchor is the segment split, not total sales: CPO revenue was IDR29.7bn in the nine months to September 2026 [S6, note 38] and the other IDR33.3bn was palm kernel and shell. At the 2026 CPO deck, the realisation ratio and the IDR rate that ratio was earned at, the CPO line implies a nine-month CPO volume of 1.8 kt, a twelve-month run-rate of 2.4 kt CPO. The fourth quarter of 2025 was the *weakest* quarter of that year: the nine-month revenue and the annual total in the quarterly filing leave a final quarter smaller than any of the three before it [S6, F5], so we carry no fourth-quarter uplift into the run-rate.

Volume is then held flat, at 2.4 kt CPO in FY2030E as in FY2026E. The core area of 4,743.6 ha and plasma area of 4,965.7 ha under the PIR-Trans KKPA scheme, and the mill's 30.0 t FFB/hour capacity, explain what the asset could process; they existed in FY2025, when the same estate produced 13.9 kt CPO of CPO, so they do not explain why the collapsed crop returns [S6, S5]. The FY2026 net-sales target in the annual report is the same target the company missed in FY2025, at IDR246.4bn realised against it [S5]. No contract, FFB-supply agreement or management plan in the archived filings supports a recovery, so a recovery sits in the bull case, not the base.

Palm kernel and shell revenue is carried at IDR42.0bn, the nine-month actual grossed to a full year on the FY2025 nine-month share, and held flat with volume because the by-product follows the same crop [S6]. Realisation is flat at 83.2% of the CPO deck, the FY2025A actual — no improvement from the discount, and no further haircut [S5, S0]. Cash cost per tonne is 16,100,000.0 USD/t, which is 9M 2026 cost of goods sold of IDR49.7bn less the IDR20.9bn depreciation add-back, divided by the CPO volume produced in the same nine months — a consistent period, at the same unit cash cost FY2025 ran at, then escalated with IDR inflation [S6, S4].

**Costs and margins.** The pivot is visible in the margin structure. FY2025 gross margin was -1.4% on the purchased-FFB model; the nine months to September 2026 show a positive gross margin for the first time in the period we cover, and our FY2026E base carries 20.6% [S4, S6]. EBITDA margin is 23.0% but EBIT margin only -9.3%, because D&A of IDR26.3bn is a fixed straight-line charge on a mill and plantation estate that was built for a much larger crop [S4]. G&A is largely fixed at around the 9M 2026 run-rate, so it consumes IDR24.4bn on the smaller revenue base [S6]. There is no operating leverage in the base: the fixed D&A and G&A charge now sits on revenue of IDR81.7bn against IDR246.4bn in FY2025A, so EBIT stays negative (IDR-7.6bn) even with EBITDA positive at IDR18.8bn [S4, S6].

**Cash flow and balance sheet.** Capex of IDR0.3bn is minimal, matching the FY2025 purchase of fixed assets [S4, F22]; FCFF is IDR10.0bn, positive only because the working-capital build of IDR9.0bn is smaller than EBITDA less capex. Operating cash flow was negative in the nine months to September 2026, when the cash-flow statement shows net cash used in operating activities of IDR-22.3bn [S6]. Net debt stands at IDR141.0bn against forecast equity of IDR99.4bn (actual equity at 30 September 2026 was IDR105.7bn [S6]), and bank loans were IDR140.8bn at a contractual cost of debt of 8.2% [S4]. There is no dividend (the policy permits dividends only when retained earnings are positive, which they are not; retained‑earnings losses exceeded IDR121.6bn at end‑2025 [S5]) and no buyback [S4, S5]. The debt‑equity ratio combined with negative FCFF leaves little room for error: a covenant breach or a rise in the bank‑rate spread would force either a capital raise (dilutive) or a shareholder‑to‑debt conversion (also dilutive). The cash‑flow‑to‑debt‑service ratio is far below one, because operating cash flow is negative, so any default would have to be cured by out‑of‑pocket cash from a shareholder — an event we treat as the bull case, not the base.

**Earnings-quality flags.** The reported net loss includes a large deferred‑tax charge and one‑off other income (a reversal of a receivable allowance worth IDR12.5bn), so headline numbers flatter the operating performance; the accruals ratio is distorted by deferred tax and the receivable reversal [S4]. Additionally, the board wrote off IDR34.4bn of other receivables as uncollectible by resolution of 30 December 2025, against 9M 2026 equity of IDR105.7bn [S6, note 9] — a one-off extinguishment of third-party claims that no accruals ratio captures but that defines how much of the receivable book was ever collectible. Related‑party flows are not disclosed as a large share of revenue, but the ownership concentration and the October 2026 change of controller are structure flags [S6; press]. Land title is a governance exposure that no earnings metric captures: the core HGU certificates are pledged to the Bank Permata facility and the plasma area's title chain is not evidenced in the filings we read [S6, S5]. The cash‑flow statement for 9M 2026 shows net cash used in operating activities of IDR-22.3bn, materially different from the net loss of IDR-12.9bn, because of the large annual D&A charge: once the company extinguishes its accumulated losses, a similar divergence would surface in the earnings‑quality screen.

We use a life-of-asset DCF at through-cycle CPO prices as the primary method, because Andira's value is the present value of a depleting, price-taking processing asset, not a multiple of a normalised earnings stream it does not currently earn (commodity-producer method card). The build gives a cost of equity of 13.3% and a WACC of 11.3%, from an unlevered beta of 0.80, the house emerging-market ERP and a country-risk premium [S0]. Levering gives 1.12 at a net debt to equity of 0.52, giving a debt weight of 34.2% and an equity weight of 65.8%. The pretax cost of debt in the WACC is 9.4% (IDR risk-free rate of 7.4% plus the house macro deck's corporate debt spread) [S0 deck]. That market borrowing cost sits above the 8.2% contractual coupon on the Bank Permata facility, which we use for the interest forecast; the difference between the two rates is the house macro deck's corporate spread, not a company-specific adjustment [S0 deck, S4]. The WACC is therefore dominated by the cost of equity, which is what a small, illiquid, loss-making processor should carry.

The explicit forecast runs to FY2035E against the house CPO deck (1,135.0 USD/t for FY2026E, 1,210.0 USD/t for FY2028E, settling to a long-run marker of 1,150.0 USD/t), with cash costs escalated by IDR inflation and terminal growth of 3.3% [S0]. The DCF enterprise value is IDR201.5bn; after net debt the equity value is Rp7 per share. The terminal value is 46.8% of the DCF value, which is high for a no-moat processor: it reflects a long-lived asset base and a forecast that does not reach a normalised plateau, and it is the part of the valuation most exposed to the volume path.

The cross-checks disagree, and the disagreement is the point. The EV/EBITDA method at 22.0x applied to the small positive base-case EBITDA of IDR18.8bn produces a value that adds nothing the DCF and P/B do not already carry: the earnings stream is depressed by a fixed D&A charge built for a larger crop, so an earnings multiple on it double-counts the same information. We therefore zero-weight it, own that the blend is carried by two methods, and say so rather than pretend a third exists. On P/BV at 1.3x (the plantation-peer median) the value is Rp14, 114.9% above the DCF: book equity carries the mill and mature plantations at historical cost [S4], but the DCF says the future cash flows from those assets are less than their depreciation charge. That is the 114.9% P/B-versus-DCF divergence. We weight the DCF at 80.0% because cash flow is what matters for a processor that earns below its cost of capital, give P/B a 20.0% weight as a trading-multiple check that the DCF is not wholly detached from balance-sheet reality, and zero-weight EV/EBITDA, giving a base-case value of Rp9; weighting the scenarios at their probabilities then gives the Rp11 twelve-month target. The P/B cross-check is a mark-to-market, not a floor: book value could be written down if HGU renewal or the plasma-land title chain fails, and it is encumbered by debt secured on the HGU certificates; a liquidation would start at a large discount [S5, S4, S6].

The sensitivity table shows the target is most sensitive to the CPO price and the volume recovery: the grid's first step away from the deck lifts the base value by roughly half, and no point in the grid recovers the current share price. What today's price implies: at Rp29 the market is capitalising 2.7x book and assuming either a return to the old volume or a recapitalisation. The reverse DCF says the current price requires the CPO benchmark to sit at 2,092.6 USD/t in FY2027E, 1.7x the deck's FY2027E value of 1,240.0 USD/t (1,150.0 USD/t as the long-run marker) [S0]. Neither that price, nor a return to the old volume, is the most likely path, which is why the target sits below the price rather than at the liquidator's book value.

**Downside risks.** (i) *Refinancing* (high likelihood, high impact): IDR140.8bn of bank debt against IDR1.4bn of cash and negative operating cash flow means the facility maturity in February 2029 must be refinanced; a covenant breach or higher‑than‑contracted spread is the most direct path to equity dilution [S4]. (ii) *FFB supply* (high, high): the mill's utilisation depends on nucleus, plasma and third‑party growers, and the company acknowledges 'shortages or delays' resulting in suboptimal processing [S5]. (iii) *CPO price* (medium, high): a fall to the deck's long‑run marker of 1,150.0 USD/t or below cuts revenue on a dollar‑for‑dollar basis [S0]. (iv) *Land title* (medium, high): the core estate's HGU certificates are pledged to the Bank Permata facility and the titles run to a fixed term, while the plasma area is farmed by smallholders; renewal and the plasma title chain are the exposure, not an absence of title [S6, S5]. (v) *Governance/control* (medium, medium): the October 2026 change of controller (Puncak Jaya Sejahtera reported to have bought the Central Energi Pratama block) could bring either support or related‑party leakage; neither is priced [S6; press]. (vi) *Liquidity* (medium, medium): the free float is 31.2% and average daily volume is IDR2,674,797,815.9bn, thinner than many IDX small‑caps [S0]. (vii) *Earnings-quality* (medium, medium): the reported net loss includes a large deferred‑tax charge and one‑off other income (receivable reversal of IDR12.5bn), which flattens the operating performance; the accruals ratio is distorted [S4]. The IDR34.4bn write-off of third-party other receivables in December 2025 shows how much of the receivable book was never collected, and no source we archived reconciles it to the reversal [S6].

**Bear/base/bull.** In the bear (probability 25.0%) CPO trades below the deck, volume runs below the already-shrunken base, unit cash cost runs above plan, and the 2029 facility is refinanced at a meaningfully wider spread — the last being the channel through which a covenant breach or negative operating cash flow (IDR-22.3bn in 9M 2026, against 8.2% contractual debt service on the opening balance [S4]) becomes a dilutive capital raise or a debt-to-equity conversion; the equity is worth Rp3. In the base (50.0%) the post-pivot business holds flat: the shrunken crop, flat by-product revenue, the fixed D&A and G&A charges and the contractual cost of debt, and the equity is worth Rp9. In the bull (25.0%) CPO trades above the deck on a tight-year price, the new owner restores part of the lost FFB supply and volume runs materially above the flat base — still a fraction of the FY2025 crop — unit cash cost runs below plan and the facility is refinanced at a narrower spread, and the equity is worth Rp23. The bear and bull shocks are mirrored on the same four drivers (CPO deck, volume, unit cash cost, cost of debt), as the method card requires; the base carries the most probable path, which is the post-pivot business, not the old trading volume. We assign the most probable weight to the base and equal smaller weights to the tails because the control-change execution is unproven, but the underlying asset (PIR-Trans KKPA licence, mill) is real and could be monetised even at less than economic returns [S6, S5]. The bull price is a supply-shock tail above the deck, not a deck forecast: it is the El Nino and B50 supply-risk channel the sector prices from time to time, and it is mirrored by the bear's discount to the deck, so neither tail is calibrated to a single year's outcome [S0, S5]. A separate book-impairment shock on the land title is not run, for a stated reason: the DCF, not book, carries most of the blend, so a writedown of land and mature plantations would reach the target only through the P/B cross-check; we flag it as an unquantified downside rather than invent a number for it [S5, S4].

**Signposts that would change the view.** A registered exchange filing showing new‑owner capital injection or a debt‑to‑equity swap; a return of third‑party FFB supply with disclosed volumes; an HGU renewal or a plasma-land title resolution; any FY2026 audited EBITDA above our base; and a clarification of the controller’s identity and strategy (Puncak Jaya Sejahtera) would move the needle. Conversely, a covenant‑waiver request, a going‑concern paragraph in the FY2026 audit, or a disclosure of a default on the bank facility would confirm the bear.

Ownership is concentrated: Central Energi Pratama held the largest block and Anugerah Perkasa Semesta the second before the October 2026 change; the free float is 31.2% and insiders hold 59.0% [S0, S6]. The new controller, Puncak Jaya Sejahtera, is reported in the press to have bought the controlling block from Central Energi Pratama; the company's disclosure page lists no filing on the transfer (press, not filed) [S7]. There is no evidence of a mandatory tender offer or of a capital injection.

Related-party dealings are not disclosed as a large share of revenue in the FY2025 notes, but the related-party note does list affiliate balances and the company is controlled through a small number of holding vehicles, so the flow is unquantified rather than shown to be immaterial; we treat it as a structure flag [S4, S6]. The December 2025 board resolution writing off IDR34.4bn of third-party other receivables against 9M 2026 equity of IDR105.7bn is the single most important governance fact in the current filing: it extinguished claims worth a substantial part of equity, and in the sections we read of the note the resolution is not accompanied by a counterparty breakdown [S6]. The FY2025 accounts were audited by KAP Sabar and Partners, which gave the opinion that they present fairly in all material respects; the annual report carries a going-concern section that records continuing losses in both years, so the clean opinion does not cure the liquidity risk [S5, S4]. The dividend record is empty: no dividend in the years covered by the data pack [S0, S4].

ESG exposures are typical for Indonesian palm oil: land-use and peat, labour practices, and the social licence around plasma growers. The company states that it has no plantation inside forest areas and describes sustainability programmes, but the disclosure is thin and not independently assured in the sections we read [S5]. For a small processor, the material ESG risk is the social licence with FFB suppliers and the plasma-land title chain, both of which are also commercial risks [S5, S6].

Dated catalysts: the FY2026 audited accounts (March 2027) will show whether the 9M 2026 margin holds; any new-controller funding or debt-restructuring announcement (no date); and the monthly CPO reference price, which sets the realised price with a lag [S0]. We monitor four KPIs: CPO volume and the FFB supply mix, the realised price versus the deck, cash cost per tonne, and the net-debt/EBITDA trajectory [S4, S6]. A second consecutive set of accounts with positive gross profit but a loss driven by depreciation and interest rather than by the product mix would confirm that the fixed-cost base, not sourcing, is the binding constraint.

We also watch the quarterly LK for any change in the ownership block or a disclosure around the reported controller change [S6], the bank facility note for covenant headroom and maturity [S4], and the annual report for progress on land title and plasma-area additions [S5]. The single most informative item would be a company statement on FY2027 volume and capital expenditure; without one, the volume path in this report remains our estimate from the nine-month actuals, not a company plan. Any of the signposts above landing on the wrong side would push us to the bear case rather than to a lower base case, because the base already assumes no recovery, and the filings do not support one.

S0.title: Yahoo Finance statements, prices and profile for ANDI.JK

bear.narrative: CPO trades a quarter below the deck through the forecast, the FFB supply collapse continues so volume runs three-tenths below the flat base, unit cash cost runs above plan on fixed-cost absorption, and the 2029 facility is refinanced at a spread a third wider — the channel through which a covenant breach becomes a dilutive capital raise.

bull.narrative: CPO trades a third above the deck on the El Nino supply loss and the B50 biodiesel mandate, a new-owner recapitalisation restores part of the lost FFB supply and lifts volume two-fifths above the flat base — still a fraction of the FY2025 crop — unit cash cost runs below plan, and the facility is refinanced at a narrower spread.

assumptions.label: CPO sales volume plan
assumptions.basis: Rebuilt from the segment split in note 38 (S6): CPO revenue IDR29.738bn and palm kernel IDR33.327bn in the nine months to September 2026. At the 2026 CPO deck of USD1,135/t, realisation 0.832 and USD/IDR 17,570, the implied CPO volume is 1.79 kt in nine months. Q4-2025 was the weakest quarter at 20.6% of the year (S6, F5), so there is no seasonal uplift to assume; FY2026E is the twelve-month run-rate of 2.39 kt. We hold volume flat through the forecast: the 4,744 ha core and 4,966 ha plasma area (F36, F37) and the 30 t FFB/hour mill (F38) explain what the asset could produce, not why a crop that fell to a seventh of FY2025 returns, and the IDR300bn FY2026 target in the annual report (S5) is the same target the company missed in 2025 at 82.1% realisation (S5). No contract, FFB-supply agreement or company plan in the archived filings supports a recovery, so it sits in the bull case, not the base.

assumptions.label: Realised price / benchmark
assumptions.basis: Calibrated on the last full actual, not on a forecast spike. FY2025A CPO segment revenue of IDR 191.237bn (F3) over 13.873 kt (F2) gives an ASP of IDR 13.785m/t; at the FY2025 usd_idr of 16,448 that is USD 838/t against the FY2025 CPO deck of USD 1,007/t, a ratio of 0.832. The discount reflects the domestic refiner customer base and South Sumatra location. Held flat; no further haircut or premium assumed.

assumptions.label: Share of volume under a price cap (e.g. DMO)
assumptions.basis: engine default constant; no domestic price cap applies to CPO

assumptions.label: Strip ratio (bcm per tonne) or cost-intensity factor
assumptions.basis: Plantation has no overburden analogue; the cost-intensity factor is 1.0 and all cash cost sits in cost_per_bcm (S4).

assumptions.label: Cash cost per tonne of CPO (IDR/t)
assumptions.basis: Rebuilt from the 9M-2026 actuals on a consistent period: cash COGS of IDR28.797bn (F30 − F35) over the observed CPO volume of 1.79 kt yields IDR16.1m/t. Annualised cash COGS at the same run‑rate is IDR38.4bn; divided by the FY2026E volume of 2.39 kt that is IDR16.1m/t again, because the fixed‑cost element is small at this scale. FY2025 cash cost was IDR15.8m/t (IDR219.6bn cash COGS / 13.87 kt), so the unit cost is unchanged; the gross‑margin improvement came from selling the third‑party purchase margin down, not from a lower per‑tonne cash cost (S6, S4). We hold the per‑tonne cash cost at IDR16.1m/t and escalate with IDR inflation.

assumptions.label: Fuel share of mining cost
assumptions.basis: engine default constant

assumptions.label: Other cash cost per unit (haul, barge, process)
assumptions.basis: Zero: all cash cost is captured in cost_per_bcm (strip_ratio 1.0); freight is netted in the realised price.

assumptions.label: Royalty rate (flat regimes)
assumptions.basis: Zero. The FY2025 cost-of-revenue note has no royalty, export-levy or export-duty line (S4); the company sells CPO and PK to domestic refiners and PK processors (S5), so the export levy borne by exporters is not part of its cost base. No harvest tax is charged in the LK.

assumptions.label: Other revenue (palm kernel and shell)
assumptions.basis: Palm kernel and shell revenue observed in 9M‑2026: IDR33.327bn (S6 note 38), which is 52.8% of net sales and, at 1.79 kt of CPO, IDR18.6bn per kt of CPO. Grossed up on the FY2025 nine-month share of 79.4% it is IDR42.0bn for FY2026E. The line is held flat with volume; the by-product follows the same crop, so a flat volume means flat kernel and shell revenue.

assumptions.label: Gross margin on other revenue
assumptions.basis: Set to 1.0 (no cost against the line) because the cash cost of producing the kernel and shell is already inside cost_per_bcm: the 9M-2026 segment note allocates the whole cost of goods sold of IDR49.699bn to the CPO segment and reports the palm-kernel segment with no cost of sales (S6 note 38). The engine computes other cost of revenue as other_revenue x (1 - margin), so a full margin here is what avoids double counting. It is an allocation convention, not a claim that the by-product is free to produce.

assumptions.label: D&A per unit (IDR/t CPO)
assumptions.basis: Total D&A is fixed in nominal IDR, not proportional to volume. FY2025 total D&A was IDR30.371bn (fixed-asset depreciation 19.525 + mature-plantation depreciation 8.060 + land-rights amortisation 1.905 + opex depreciation 0.881; F13) and the 9M-2026 cash-flow add-back was IDR20.902bn (F35), a full-year run-rate of IDR26.3bn. Spread over the FY2026E volume of 2.39 kt that is IDR11.02m/t. Because volume is held flat, the per-tonne charge is flat in nominal terms; the annual charge does not change with the forecast.

assumptions.label: Sustaining capex per unit (IDR/t CPO)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 purchase of fixed assets was IDR 1.663bn (F22) on 13.873 kt, or IDR 119,901/t; FY2024 was IDR 4.772bn (F23). Held at the FY2025 level and escalated with IDR inflation. The 9M-2026 accounts show no expansion programme and no material capital commitment disclosed (S6, S4).

assumptions.label: Other capex (expansion projects)
assumptions.basis: Zero: no expansion, replanting or mill project is disclosed or committed in the FY2025 accounts or the 9M-2026 LK (S4, S6).

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Net working capital at 30 September 2026 was IDR 10.236bn on a revenue run-rate of about IDR 84bn, or 12% of revenue (S0 pack balance sheet, S6 revenue). FY2025 was near zero (IDR 0.525bn), so the 2026 build is a step change; we hold 11% of revenue, which captures the observed build and assumes no release.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: No current tax: FY2025 current tax was nil, the deferred tax charge of IDR 15.991bn was non-cash (F25), and the company carries a fiscal loss (S4). Modelled at zero until the accumulated tax losses are exhausted; no tax shield value is credited beyond that.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: The Bank Permata facility bears 8.25% per annum, matures 13 February 2029 and had a ceiling of IDR 386bn (S4, note 21). FY2025 interest expense of IDR 12.10bn on opening debt of IDR 149.888bn was 8.07%; the 8.25% contractual rate is used.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_income, cash[-1]))

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Zero: the facility is amortising (bank loans fell from IDR 148.2bn to IDR 140.7bn in FY2025) and no new facility is disclosed (S4).

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Zero: FY2025 other income of IDR 13.985bn was one-off (IDR 12.5bn receivable-allowance reversal, IDR 1.09bn employee-benefit reversal, asset-disposal gain) and is not repeated (S4).

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A; the accounts show no minority interest on the balance sheet (S4).

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: No dividend for FY2023 or FY2024, and the policy permits a dividend only when retained earnings are positive (S5). With accumulated losses of IDR 121.564bn at end-2025 (S5) no dividend is modelled in the forecast period.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Zero: 9,350,000,000 shares outstanding and no rights issue or buyback announced (F24, S5).

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: IDR long-run inflation of 3.3% (house macro deck cpi_id), consistent with the cost and price escalation in the explicit period; no real growth after FY2035E.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: 9M-2026 operating expenses were IDR18.835bn on revenue of IDR63.065bn, or 29.9% (F32, F29); FY2025 G&A was IDR23.994bn on IDR246.4bn, 9.7% (F11, F5). The charge is fixed in absolute terms, so the ratio is 29.9% on the shrunken 2026 revenue and would fall only if revenue recovered, which the base case does not. We hold 29.9% flat, so the model does not credit operating leverage the filings do not evidence; it is the ratio that reproduces the last actual.

challenges.challenge: The volume anchor is built on a misread revenue split. The volume basis says "9M-2026 CPO revenue is about four-fifths of net sales of IDR 63.065bn". S6 note 25 and the segment note split 9M-2026 revenue into CPO IDR29.738bn and PK/shell IDR33.327bn (they sum exactly to IDR63.065bn [S6]), so CPO is ~47% of sales, not ~80%. At the FY2026 CPO deck of USD1,135/t, 0.832 realisation and ~IDR16.5k/USD, IDR29.738bn implies ~1.9 kt of CPO sold in nine months (not 3.2 kt), i.e. ~2.6-2.8 kt for FY2026, not 4.5 kt. The 4.5 -> 6.6 kt path, which the report itself calls a top-two value driver, is overstated by roughly 60-70%. The model partly hides this because other_revenue (PK/shell) is set at IDR18bn while actual 9M-2026 PK/shell revenue alone is IDR33.3bn (~IDR44bn annualised).
challenges.answer: Rebuilt volume from the S6 segment note: CPO revenue of IDR29.738bn is 47% of net sales, not four-fifths. At the FY2026 CPO deck of USD1,135/t, 0.832 realisation and 9M USD/IDR 17,570, the implied CPO volume is 1.79 kt in nine months (F51), so FY2026E is 2.39 kt on a flat path. Q4-2025 was the weakest quarter at 20.6% of the year, so no seasonal uplift. No contract, FFB-supply agreement or company plan in the filings supports a recovery, so it sits in the bull case.

challenges.challenge: The IDR6.8m/t cash cost is an arithmetic error. Cost_per_bcm basis takes 9M-2026 cash COGS of IDR28.797bn (nine months) and divides it by a full-year FY2026E volume of 4.5 kt to get 6.8m/t. Nine months of cash COGS cannot be spread over twelve months of volume. Annualised, the same run-rate is ~IDR38.4bn, or ~8.5m/t at 4.5 kt; on the ~1.9 kt of CPO actually sold in 9M-2026 it is ~15.2m/t, close to the FY2025 cash cost of IDR15.8m/t [S6, S4]. The DCF therefore carries a cost base roughly 25-55% too low, and the calibration.ebitda gap is a symptom of it.
challenges.answer: Fixed the unit-cost arithmetic: 9M cash COGS of IDR28.797bn over the same nine-month CPO volume of 1.79 kt gives IDR16.1m/t, and annualised cash COGS of IDR38.4bn over FY2026E volume of 2.39 kt gives the same IDR16.1m/t. FY2025 cash cost was IDR15.8m/t, so the unit cost is consistent rather than structurally lower. The DCF now carries that cost base and the calibration gap is explained by the fixed opex ratio.

challenges.challenge: The FY2026 volume bridge relies on a seasonality claim the filing contradicts. The basis says "a seasonally stronger fourth quarter (Q4-2025 revenue was the strongest quarter of that year)". S6 gives 9M-2025 revenue of IDR195.631bn against FY2025 of IDR246.430bn [S6, F5], so Q4-2025 was IDR50.799bn, or 20.6% of the year, i.e. the weakest quarter, not the strongest. Using a Q4 uplift to lift 9M volume of ~1.9 kt to 4.5 kt is unsupported; on the actual Q4-2025 share the FY2026 figure would be lower still.
challenges.answer: Corrected the seasonality claim: S6 shows FY2025 revenue of IDR246.430bn against 9M-2025 of IDR195.631bn, so Q4-2025 was IDR50.799bn, the weakest quarter at 20.6% of the year, not the strongest. The volume bridge no longer relies on a Q4-2025 uplift; FY2026E is the twelve-month run-rate of the nine-month volume, with no assumption of a Q4 rebound.

challenges.challenge: The drift.volume justification is not evidence of recovery. It cites 5,250 ha of permitted core area and a 30 t FFB/hour mill, but those existed in FY2025 when the same asset produced 13.9 kt CPO and collapsed to ~2 kt; area and throughput explain capability, not why volume returns. It also cites "management's FY2026 net-sales guidance is IDR 300bn [S5]", but S5 page 99 shows a Rp300bn 2026 target and page 98 shows the identical Rp300bn target for 2025 was missed at 82.14% realisation (IDR246.43bn). A target the company has already missed is not a credible recovery plan. The cited "5,250 ha" is also not F36 (4,743.56 ha) and not the 30-Jun-2026 planted core of 4,943.52 ha [S6].
challenges.answer: Replaced the capacity and target argument: the 4,744 ha core, 4,966 ha plasma and 30 t FFB/hour mill existed in FY2025 when output was 13.9 kt, so they explain capability, not why a seventh of that crop returns. The IDR300bn FY2026 net-sales target is the same target the company missed in FY2025 at 82.1% realisation. No sourced recovery mechanism exists in the filings, so volume is held flat and the drift is the volume collapse itself.

challenges.challenge: Method weighting does work the text refuses to defend. §4 says EV/EBITDA at 5.83x is "not meaningful" because "EBITDA is negative in the base", but the base-case FY2026E EBITDA is +IDR20.64bn; only EBIT is negative (-IDR7.9bn). The method is nonetheless given a 25% weight and a value of zero, which lowers the 60/25/15 blend from ~IDR23 to ~IDR19 and the 12-month target from ~IDR24 to IDR20. Either the multiple is meaningful (then defend 5.83x and 25%) or it is not (then zero-weight it and own the higher target). As written it is a hidden bearish input with a false justification.
challenges.answer: Corrected the base-case EBITDA statement: it is positive, not negative. Zero-weighted the EV/EBITDA method because a multiple adds nothing the DCF and P/B do not already carry when earnings are depressed by fixed D&A built for a larger crop. The blend is now 80% DCF and 20% P/B, so the target is not dragged by a hidden zero that the text disowned.

challenges.challenge: The P/B anchor is inverted. §4 applies 1.5x book (9M-2026 BVPS ~IDR11.30 x 1.51 = IDR17) and calls it a "floor", while the paragraph argues the DCF is below book because "the assets are worth less than the balance sheet shows". If the assets are worth less than book, a liquidator recovers below 1x book, not 1.5x. A genuine liquidation/NAV cross-check would sit near or below book and pull the blend down, not up. Using 1.5x as the "honest bull anchor" both contradicts the thesis and flatters the target.
challenges.answer: Revised the P/B rationale: it is a trading-multiple cross-check, not a floor. Book carries the mill and mature plantations at historical cost while the DCF says their future cash flows are worth less than the depreciation charge, so the DCF sits below book. The plantation-peer median multiple at a 20% weight is a market cross-check, and the report now says explicitly that a liquidation would start at a discount to book rather than at a premium.

challenges.challenge: Several load-bearing figures are wrong in the prose. §1 says "CPO revenue of IDR250.0bn against IDR55.2bn for PK and shells in FY2025"; F3 and F28 put FY2025 CPO revenue at IDR191.237bn (IDR250.0bn is the FY2025 COGS, F7). §3 says "Revenue fell from IDR196.7bn in FY2024A to IDR246.4bn in FY2025A" (it rose). §3 puts equity at IDR99.7bn, while F43 shows 9M-2026 equity of IDR105.690bn. §3 also writes "30.0 kt CPO of FFB per hour" where the mill is 30 t FFB/hour (F38).
challenges.answer: Fixed the load-bearing figures: FY2025 CPO revenue is IDR191.237bn (F48), not the COGS line; revenue rose from FY2024 to FY2025 (F5, F6); equity at 30 September 2026 is IDR105.690bn (F43); and the mill is 30 t FFB/hour, not 30 kt of CPO. Each now carries the correct fact placeholder rather than a typed number.

challenges.challenge: The bear does not run the risk the report spends a paragraph describing. §3 states cash-flow-to-debt-service is "far below one" and a covenant breach or higher spread "would force either a capital raise (dilutive) or a shareholder-to-debt conversion (also dilutive)". The bear narrative repeats a higher 2029 refinancing rate, but the shocks are only d.agri.cpo x0.8, a.volume x0.95 and a.cost_per_bcm x1.1 - no cost_of_debt, net_borrowing or share-change shock. For a company with 9M-2026 OCF of -IDR22.3bn (F34), the dilution/refinancing channel is the dominant downside and it is unmodelled.
challenges.answer: Added the refinancing channel the narrative describes: the bear now shocks cost_of_debt to 1.3x the contractual 8.25%, so a higher spread on the 2029 maturity flows through interest and FCFF. That is the path from the negative operating cash flow of IDR22.3bn in 9M-2026 to a dilutive raise or debt-to-equity conversion, and it is now run in the bear value.

challenges.challenge: Two governance facts in S6 are absent. First, the company wrote off IDR34.376bn of third-party other receivables as uncollectible (S6, board resolution 30 Dec 2025) - ~33% of 9M-2026 equity - yet the earnings-quality section mentions only the IDR12.5bn allowance reversal (F41). Second, the report says book is a floor "only if the HGU title ... is resolved", but the bear has no land-rights impairment or book-value writedown, even though the equity value it defends is largely land and mature plantations.
challenges.answer: Added the IDR34.376bn write-off of third-party other receivables (S6 note 9, board resolution of 30 December 2025) to the earnings-quality and governance flags, alongside the allowance reversal, and kept related-party flows as an unquantified structure flag. The HGU/book-impairment shock is not run and the report states why: the DCF carries most of the blend, so a writedown reaches the target only through the P/B cross-check.

challenges.challenge: The bull case is far smaller than the upside the report itself names. The summary says the strongest case against the rating is "a new-owner recapitalisation that restores third-party FFB supply and lifts volume back toward the mill's capacity"; the bull only shocks volume x1.05. The estate (4,943.52 ha planted core as of 30 Jun 2026, 4,965.68 ha plasma [S6]) at a national ~3.5 t CPO/ha supports ~17 kt, and FY2025 alone was 13.9 kt. A recapitalisation case is multiples of the +5% assumed, so either the bull is materially understated or the summary overstates the upside.
challenges.answer: Aligned the bull with its narrative: volume is shocked 1.4x the flat base, which is 3.35 kt against 13.9 kt in FY2025, so the recapitalisation case is materially larger than the old 1.05x while still a fraction of the old crop. The investment summary is rewritten to that magnitude rather than to the mill's capacity, and no capital injection is assumed because no filing discloses one.

challenges.challenge: The bull caps CPO at +20% (x1.2) while its own narrative invokes the GAPKI 2026-11-12 warning that El Nino could cut national 2027 output by up to 3m tonnes and the B50 mandate. A supply loss of that size is a price tail larger than x1.2; the cap is not sourced to the deck.
challenges.answer: Widened the bull CPO shock to 1.3x the deck from 1.2x, and made the bear mirror it at 0.75x, which the engine's log-symmetry test passes. The report now states plainly that the bull price is a supply-shock tail above the deck rather than a deck forecast, with the El Nino and B50 channel named and the deck's long-run marker bounding the bear [S0, S5].

challenges.challenge: The calibration.ebitda justification assumes a permanent change in sourcing ("the mill bought third-party FFB at market" in FY2025 vs a 46%-of-sales cash COGS in 9M-2026) but cites no statement that the company will not resume third-party purchases. The 9M-2026 evidence is lower volume and lower COGS, which is equally consistent with a temporary demand/supply contraction at the same unit economics (~15m/t). The 1,800% gap is therefore not reconciled to the filing; it is reconciled to an unproven assumption.
challenges.answer: Answered the calibration gap on mechanics, not on an unproven sourcing change: the unit cash cost is held at the observed IDR16.1m/t and the FY2025 repricing gap comes from the template's revenue-ratio opex, a fixed charge of about IDR24bn that becomes 29.9% of the shrunken revenue. No structural sourcing shift is assumed anywhere in the base case, and the FY2026E EBITDA is lower as a result.

missing_bull_case.note: Bull only shocks volume +5%, yet the summary says the strongest case is a recapitalisation lifting volume "back toward the mill's capacity". The new controller (Puncak Jaya Sejahtera, press) and a return toward FY2025's 13.9 kt are not in any run; the physical estate (4,943 ha planted, 30 t FFB/hr [S6, S5]) supports far more than 6.6 kt.

missing_bear_case.note: The bear narrative cites a higher 2029 refinancing rate but the shocks list has no cost_of_debt or dilution shock, so the stated risk is not run. 9M-2026 OCF is -IDR22.3bn (F34) against interest of ~IDR7.9bn; the HGU title risk and a book-value impairment are not in the bear either.

assumption_realism.note: Volume 4.5 -> 6.6 kt (+47%) is sourced to physical capacity that already existed in FY2025 when volume was 13.9 kt and to the IDR300bn target the company already missed in 2025 (realisation 82.1% [S5]). Area and mill throughput explain capability, not why a collapsed volume recovers.

evidence_and_citations.note: Key inputs checked: F29/F30/F31/F34/F35 hold in S6, and the FY2025 CPO revenue of IDR191.237bn holds (F3). But the volume basis misreads 9M-2026 CPO revenue as ~four-fifths of sales when S6 note 25 splits it at IDR29.738bn (~47%), and §1 quotes CPO revenue as IDR250.0bn (that is the COGS figure).

valuation_method_fit.note: DCF is primary per the commodity card, but 25% of the blend sits on an EV/EBITDA value of zero that §4 calls "not meaningful" and justifies with the false statement that base EBITDA is negative (it is +IDR20.6bn). P/B at 1.5x is applied as a "floor" although the report argues the assets are worth less than book.

bias_and_tone.note: The target is dragged below the DCF by a 25%-weighted zero EV/EBITDA that the text disowns; dropping it would lift the base blend from ~19 to ~23 and the target toward ~24. The prose also conflates EBIT and EBITDA ("EBITDA is negative in the base") and says revenue "fell" from 196.7 to 246.4.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: CPO deck, USD/IDR, CPI and terminal growth are read from the house decks; royalty flat-zero is consistent with the audited cost-of-revenue note (no royalty/levy line [S4]) and the domestic-sales model.

conservatism_audit.note: A -68% volume cut from the FY2025 actual is unsourced beyond "the 9M-2026 run-rate" and an unproven permanent sourcing shift; the unit cost of IDR6.8m/t divides nine months of cash COGS by a full-year volume, understating the real ~15m/t. Both are unexplained departures from the last actual in the bearish direction.

calibration.note: The 1,800% calibration gap is answered by asserting a permanent mix change, but 9M-2026 shows lower volume and lower COGS, not a stated policy change. The same arithmetic underlies the 6.8m/t cost, so the justification and the gap share one unverified assumption.

signoff.notes: Independently verified: BLOCK flags justified on the LK (opex restated from note 27; EBIT restated to the LK operating loss; calibration gap is a fixed-cost/revenue-ratio artifact, not a cost change); volume rebuilt from the S6 segment note and anchored at the post-pivot 9M-2026 run-rate, the most likely path given the control change and shrinking crop; scenarios bear 0.75x / bull 1.3x CPO pass log-symmetry, bull 1.4x volume sourced to the recap narrative; P/B is a 20% cross-check not a floor; earnings-quality flags include the IDR34.4bn third-party write-off and allowance reversal; target Rp11 is the probability-weighted blend, SELL vs Rp29. No broker or consensus content; every factual paragraph carries citations.

bias.note: Base is anchored on the last actual (9M-2026 annualised): volume 2.39 kt, realisation 0.832 and cash cost 16.1m/t are all calibrated to observed actuals, not haircut [S6, S4]. Recovery to the FY2025 crop sits in the bull (volume x1.4 = 3.35 kt), further decline in the bear (x0.7). No unsourced conservatism or optimism found: royalty zero is evidenced (no royalty/levy line, S4), and the only departure from company plan (IDR300bn FY2026 target) is justified by the actual 9M-2026 revenue of IDR63.1bn [S6].

findings.finding: Judge call this round returned a length-truncated skip (finish=length, no JSON verdict); no judge issues to answer.
Lint PASS with warnings: 4,566 words vs 500-3,500, and two valuation methods (EV/EBITDA zero-weighted and argued). Not a fail per owner instruction; a shorter packet would also let the judge parse.
October 2026 controller change remains press-only with no registered filing in the archive; bridge empty and post_bs_review states it. Disclosed, not a defect.

flags.message: FY+1 priced at FY2025A benchmark and volume gives EBITDA -50.8 vs the actual 2.8 (-1883%): reconcile costs, royalty or realisation with the filing, or justify the change
flags.justification: The gate re-prices FY2025 volume at the FY2026 unit cost and a revenue-ratio opex. The unit cost is consistent: FY2025 cash COGS of IDR219.6bn over 13.873 kt is IDR15.8m/t against the FY2026 assumption of IDR16.1m/t [S4, F13]. The gap is opex: the charge is fixed at about IDR24bn, which is 9.7% of FY2025 revenue of IDR246.4bn but 29.9% of the shrunken 9M-2026 revenue of IDR63.1bn [S4, S6]. The template carries opex only as a revenue ratio, so re-pricing to FY2025 volume overstates opex by roughly IDR47bn and turns a small positive EBITDA into a large negative one. The FY2026E base reproduces the actual 9M-2026 unit economics, which is the last actual [S6].

flags.message: opex FY2025A restated at 2.45x the data pack: say why the pack is wrong
flags.justification: The data pack shows IDR 9.781bn of opex, which is only the depreciation slice; the LK income statement shows general and administrative expenses of IDR 23.994bn [F11] and note 27 is the supporting disclosure [S4]. The pack understates the fixed cost base by IDR 14.2bn, so we restate from the filing.

flags.message: ebit FY2025A restated at 2.07x the data pack: say why the pack is wrong
flags.justification: The pack nets one-off other income into EBIT and shows IDR -13.311bn; the LK income statement reports an operating loss of IDR -27.524bn [F9] after G&A of IDR 23.994bn, with the IDR 13.985bn of other income presented below the operating line [S4]. We restate to the LK operating loss so that EBITDA is built from operating cash earnings.

flags.message: expected return -61%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: The view is the shrunken post-pivot crop: CPO volume falls to about 2.4 kt in FY2026E from about 13.9 kt in FY2025A, revenue to about IDR 81.7 bn from about IDR 246.4 bn, and EBITDA holds at about IDR 18.8 bn because cost falls a little faster than revenue. The equity trades at about 2.7x book against a base-case DCF value of about Rp 7 and a P/B trader mark of about Rp 14. The reverse DCF says the Rp 29 share price implies a CPO deck of about 2,092.6 USD/t in FY2027E, roughly 1.7 times the house deck of 1,240.0 USD/t. A return to the FY2025 crop is the case against us and sits in the bull scenario, not the base [S6, S5]; the rating is SELL because the market price is not yet pricing the post-pivot economics that the LK shows [S6].

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'dcf_fcff': 0.6, 'ev_ebitda': 0.25, 'pbv': 0.15}
flags.justification: EV/EBITDA is zero-weighted because the FY2026E EBITDA of IDR 20.6bn is struck after a fixed D&A charge built for a crop four times larger than the 9M-2026 run-rate [S6, S4]; a multiple on that depressed base double-counts the same fixed-cost information the DCF already carries, and the base-case EV/EBITDA value at the 5.83x peer median is not a defensible measure of this operating unit. The blend is 80% DCF (the commodity-producer primary method) and 20% P/B as a balance-sheet cross-check, so no weight rests on a method the report will not defend.
